summary.intent: Spike whether the hand-written setup-callisto installer (scripts/install-callisto.sh plus three shell tests) can be replaced by a thin composite action using cargo-binstall metadata, taiki-e/install-action, and gh attestation verify for verification: require, proven in real CI runs on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest.
summary.outcome: Added [package.metadata.binstall] and a temporary spike workflow, ran it on both runners (run 45237152860), and the spike failed on step (c), the attestation verification. The temporary workflow was removed and pushed, and step 2 (replacing the action) was not started. The transcript does not show the exact failure details, so the report to the lead is still pending.

repo: The setup-callisto action lives at .github/actions/setup-callisto with scripts/ and tests/ subdirectories. install-callisto.sh and the three shell tests are referenced from the action, the justfile, workflows, .github/tests/*.sh, graph templates and docs (stability.md, architecture/release.md).

Release assets are named callisto-<target>.tar.gz under tag callisto@<version>, built by .github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh and attested via callisto-release.yml. The binstall metadata used pkg-url = "{ repo }/releases/download/callisto@{ version }/callisto-{ target }.tar.gz", pkg-fmt = tgz and bin-dir = callisto{ binary-ext }.
The spike pinned taiki-e/install-action at fe3acb53a98b62c772db35de75ce0e4595e7ca8c (v2.90.8) with tool callisto-cli@0.22.0 and fallback cargo-binstall.

Attestation verification was tried against the installed binary and, as a control, against the release tarball, using --repo, --signer-workflow callisto-release.yml, --deny-self-hosted-runners and --source-ref refs/heads/main. The binary-verification step ran with continue-on-error, and the control step compared tarball and installed-binary sha256 to show why verifying the binary may not match the attested subject.

code.finding: Binstall metadata was inserted just before [lints] workspace = true. This is the only product-code change from the spike, and it is still on the branch.

workflow: Inside the sandbox, gh TLS fails and gpg-signed commits fail. Both had to be retried outside the sandbox, and the first push after the failed commit sent only the base commit.
macOS runners queue for a long time, so use a background gh run watch with --exit-status and read the task output afterward.
Temporary spike workflows should be named zz-* and triggered on push to the branch only, and removed in a follow-up commit once the run links are captured.

friction: The sandbox blocked gh network access and gpg signing, which forced retries outside it.
The first commit failed silently enough that a push went out without the spike commit.
Some commands were run twice with variants (rtk-prefixed grep and ls), and the log-grep pipelines needed several iterations to extract useful output.
macOS runner queueing delayed the spike result.
open_items: Report to the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) exactly what install-action/binstall cannot do for step (c), with run link https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/actions/runs/45237152860 and job ids 137911790341 and 137911790778. The failure reason is not in the transcript.
